title: Maximum Difference Between Even and Odd Frequency II
statement:
You get a string `s` made of the digits `'0'` to `'4'` and an integer `k`. Choose a substring of `s` that is at least `k` characters long, and two characters `a` and `b` such that:

- `a` occurs an odd number of times in the substring, and
- `b` occurs an even number of times in the substring, and at least once.

The substring may contain other characters as well. Return the largest possible value of (number of `a`s in the substring) minus (number of `b`s in the substring) over all such choices. The input guarantees that at least one valid choice exists.
constraints: s contains only the digits '0' to '4'
Some substring of length at least k has a character with an odd count and a character with a nonzero even count
notes:
## Intuition

Counting the digits of every substring works but costs O(n²). There are only five digits, so fix the pair: `a` is the digit with the odd count and `b` the one with the even count (20 ordered pairs). With prefix counts, the substring between prefix lengths `l` and `r` has `A[r] - A[l]` copies of `a` and `B[r] - B[l]` copies of `b`, so its difference is `(A[r] - B[r]) - (A[l] - B[l])`. For each right end we want the smallest `A[l] - B[l]` among usable left ends. "Odd count of `a`" means `A[l]` and `A[r]` have different parities, and "even count of `b`" means `B[l]` and `B[r]` have the same parity, so the minimum is kept separately for each of the four parity pairs. A left end is usable when the substring is at least `k` long and holds at least two `b`s; both stay true as the right end moves on, so each prefix is unlocked once and kept.

## Approach

1. For each ordered pair of different digits `a`, `b`, start `minDiff`, a 2 × 2 table of `Infinity`.
2. Move `right` across `s`, counting `a` and `b` in `s[0..right]` as `countA` and `countB`.
3. While the substring `s[left..right]` is at least `k` long and has at least two `b`s, store `leftA - leftB` in `minDiff[leftA % 2][leftB % 2]`, then move `left` on, updating `leftA` and `leftB`.
4. Look up `prior = minDiff[1 - countA % 2][countB % 2]`. If it is finite, `countA - countB - prior` is a candidate for `answer`.
5. Return the largest candidate over all pairs.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "12233"`, `k = 4`; follow the pair `a = 1`, `b = 3`.

- `right = 0` to `3`: `countA = 1`, but at most one `3` has been seen, so nothing is unlocked.
- `right = 4`: `countB = 2`. Prefix 0 (`leftA = 0`, `leftB = 0`) is unlocked into `minDiff[0][0] = 0`, then prefix 1 into `minDiff[1][0] = 1`; at `left = 2` the substring is too short.
- `countA = 1` is odd and `countB = 2` is even, so `prior = minDiff[0][0] = 0` and the candidate is `1 - 2 - 0 = -1`.

No other pair does better, so the answer is `-1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(20 · n) = O(n): for each of the 20 pairs, `right` and `left` each cross `s` once.
- Space: O(1): one 2 × 2 table and a few counters per pair.

## Pitfalls

- `b` must actually appear: for `s = "0001"`, `k = 1` the answer is -1, not the 3 you get by pairing three `0`s with an absent digit.
- The answer can be negative, so start `answer` at `-Infinity`, not 0.
- Unlocked prefixes are never removed: a longer substring with more `b`s is still usable, and the parity lookup does the rest.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `a`, `b` | the digit that must be odd and the digit that must be even |
| `minDiff` | `minDiff[p][q]`: smallest `leftA - leftB` over unlocked prefixes with those parities |
| `right` | index of the substring's last character |
| `countA`, `countB` | copies of `a` and `b` in `s[0..right]` |
| `left` | length of the next prefix to unlock |
| `leftA`, `leftB` | copies of `a` and `b` in `s[0..left - 1]` |
| `prior` | best unlocked prefix with the parities this right end needs |
| `answer` | largest difference found |

narration.2: No valid substring has been seen yet, and the answer may be negative.
narration.3: Try every digit as the one that must appear an odd number of times...
narration.4: ...and every digit as the one that must appear an even, nonzero number of times.
narration.5: One count is odd and the other even, so the two digits must differ.
narration.6: minDiff[p][q] keeps the smallest leftA - leftB among unlocked prefixes whose counts of a and b have parities p and q.
narration.9: Extend the substring's right end one character at a time.
narration.11: Count a in the prefix that ends at right.
narration.12: Count b in the same prefix.
narration.13: A prefix becomes usable once the substring after it is at least k long and holds at least two b's; later right ends keep it usable.
narration.16: Remember the smallest leftA - leftB for this parity pair.
narration.17: Then move past this prefix, counting the character that leaves it.
narration.19: The next prefix is one character longer.
narration.21: An odd count of a needs the opposite parity of a, and an even count of b needs the same parity of b.
narration.22: If such a prefix is unlocked...
narration.23: ...the substring between it and right gives countA - countB - prior; keep the largest.
narration.28: Return the best difference over all pairs.
